review_kind: applied-source independent review with current exhaustive-mini and sampled-real terminal proof
checks: Checkpoint begins before speculative token upload, host PLE preparation, and any target compute; rank0 owns the image and no asynchronous worker accesses it.

Every saved D2D copy is chained by the owner, and each successful copy updates Engine tail. Later writes drain the saved prefix; rollback drains compute and restores after any completed bank swap is reversed.

The plan output union explicitly includes token, position and token_history. The current plan declares token_history as an output despite PLE hash input mutation. Standalone mutable controls and FP32 scratch are covered.
Active recurrent banks and already committed QSA prefixes are deliberately not saved or overwritten. Thus illegal mutation remains visible to final-state gates and CPU negative controls.
QSA geometry matches the planner: capacity rows, ceil(capacity/4) pooled rows; rollback saves only tails after position or floor(position/4) valid rows.
Correct original allocation IDs are retained across bank selection changes; restore requires original parity and includes exact prior inactive bank bytes.

History, lookup IDs, selected experts, loaded layers, FP32 source IDs and extents are restored together. Streaming layer state must be released at checkpoint and restore; restored FP32 sources must still be live.
Sticky errors and poisoned ownership are checked before backup/restore; rollback cannot erase a target failure.

The private backup is initialized and cleared only after resolution at dump/reset/finish, and remains included in the ordinary allocation inventory. Model allocations are never scrubbed before hashing.
Engine owns the persistent backup allocation; it participates in normal admission, reset, drain and teardown. Constructor now runs before after-load memory recording, census and READY.
Rank1 allocates no rollback image. Its target token authority and asynchronous draft publication are unchanged.
CPU-only command12 corrupts an excluded active-bank or valid-QSA byte after speculation. It cannot compile into the device command handler and must cause final-state comparison failure.

Resolved boundary clears only private saved host vectors/history/parity after draining and zeroing private device backup; it does not clear live Engine metadata. Validity is false and remaining counts are explicitly telemetry.

The shared snapshot covers exactly rank0 producer bytes0..65535. Both coordinators hand over only by reading this region and writing the separate rank1 slot; rank1 publication, verifier and native mailbox lie above both slots and are never restored. Mapping stays live through restoration.
Private backup uses runtime_overhead with process lifetime, exactly matching owner.cpp planned(category); normal owner teardown still frees it after drain.
